newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish parliament lowers corporate tax from 1997.
newsitem.headline: Polish parliament lowers corporate tax from 1997.

text.p: Poland's lower house of parliament on Thursday approved a bill which provides for gradually lowering the corporate tax to 32 percent in the year 2000 from the current 40 percent.
Under the bill the tax would be cut to 38 percent as of next year and then by two points each year.

The regulation, which still needs to clear the senate and be signed by the president, also envisages a gradual reduction of tax relief for investing companies to 10 percent of the invested sum in the year 2000, from 25 percent now. @
The relief for companies which export most of their output would fall to 25 percent of the invested amount from the current 50 percent.
Tax relief would start to fall down as of 1998 under the bill, which was passed by 297 votes to 21 with 85 abstentions.
